easy.explanation: The speaker says, “Truly my soul waiteth upon God.”
easy.q: Upon whom does the speaker wait?

easy.explanation: God is called the speaker’s rock, salvation, and defence.
easy.q: How is God described in these verses?

answers: Remain standing without being greatly moved
easy.explanation: Because God is his defence, the speaker says, “I shall not be greatly moved.”
easy.q: What does trust in God enable the speaker to do?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “from him cometh my salvation.”
medium.q: What is the relationship between salvation and waiting upon God?

medium.explanation: The word “defence” describes God as the speaker’s protection.
medium.q: Which word refers to a place of protection?

answers: God is his rock and defence
medium.explanation: The speaker’s stability comes from God, who is his rock and defence.
medium.q: Why will the speaker not be greatly moved?

answers: Reliance on God rather than other supports
challenge.explanation: The verses repeatedly direct the speaker’s trust toward God alone.
challenge.q: What idea is emphasized by the repeated focus on God alone?

challenge.explanation: “Rock” suggests stability and protection, while “salvation” suggests rescue.
challenge.q: Which pair expresses both rescue and protection?

answers: Wealth is the source of security
Trust in God gives strength in danger
challenge.explanation: The speaker presents God as the source of salvation, stability, and protection.
challenge.q: What is the main idea of these verses?

paragraphs.title: Enemies and the Danger of Hypocrisy

easy.explanation: They consult to cast him down from his excellency.
easy.q: What do the enemies want to do to the man?

answers: A bowing wall and a tottering fence
easy.explanation: The passage compares them to a bowing wall and a tottering fence.
easy.q: What are the enemies compared to?

easy.explanation: They bless with their mouth but curse inwardly.
easy.q: What do the enemies hide behind their blessings?

medium.explanation: A bowing wall may collapse, suggesting danger and instability.
medium.q: What does the image of a bowing wall suggest about the enemies?

medium.explanation: The context shows that the enemies are plotting to bring the man down.
medium.q: What does “imagine mischief against a man” mean in context?

answers: They bless outwardly but curse inwardly
medium.explanation: Their outward words and inward intentions are completely different.
medium.q: What contradiction appears in the enemies’ behavior?

answers: Both have an outward appearance that hides a lack of stability
challenge.explanation: Both the structure and the hypocrites appear secure outwardly but conceal danger.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the unstable structure and hypocrisy?

challenge.explanation: Their inward cursing exposes the false nature of their outward blessing.
challenge.q: Which detail reveals that the blessings are not sincere?

answers: Harm from people who hide their intentions
challenge.explanation: The enemies conceal their hatred behind words that sound like blessings.
challenge.q: What central danger is described in the passage?

paragraphs.title: God as Refuge and Hope for All

easy.explanation: The speaker says, “my expectation is from him.”
easy.q: From whom does the speaker’s expectation come?

easy.explanation: He says, “Trust in him at all times; ye people.”
easy.q: Whom does the speaker call to trust in God?

easy.explanation: The people are told to “pour out your heart before him.”
easy.q: What does the speaker tell the people to pour out before God?

answers: Because God is a refuge for them
medium.explanation: The verse concludes, “God is a refuge for us.”
medium.q: Why does the speaker call the people to trust in God?

medium.explanation: Pouring out the heart represents honest prayer and reliance upon God.
medium.q: What does pouring out the heart before God express?

medium.explanation: God is presented as a safe place and protector for His people.
medium.q: What does “refuge” mean in this context?

answers: The speaker moves from personal trust to an appeal to all the people
challenge.explanation: The speaker first speaks of his own soul and then calls the whole people to trust God.
challenge.q: What changes in this section compared with the beginning of the psalm?

answers: Both express stability and protection from God
challenge.explanation: God gives both the speaker and the people stability and protection.
challenge.q: What connection exists between “I shall not be moved” and “a refuge for us”?

answers: Only the speaker may trust God
The people should hide their feelings
Trust in God is offered to all the people
challenge.explanation: The speaker invites all the people to trust God and pour out their hearts before Him.
challenge.q: What is the communal message of the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Emptiness of People and Wealth

easy.explanation: The passage says that men of low degree are vanity and men of high degree are a lie.
easy.q: How are people of low and high degree described?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery.”
easy.q: What does the passage warn people not to trust?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.”
easy.q: What should people not set their heart upon when riches increase?

answers: They are described as vanity and a lie
medium.explanation: The words “vanity” and “lie” show that human status is unreliable.
medium.q: Why should people not be trusted as the ultimate foundation?

medium.explanation: The verse speaks of material wealth increasing.
medium.q: What does “riches” refer to in this passage?

answers: They are all forms of prayer
They should not become the basis of trust
medium.explanation: The passage warns against making violence, theft, or wealth the foundation of confidence.
medium.q: What do oppression, robbery, and riches have in common here?

answers: They are passing and cannot provide a firm foundation
They are the source of salvation
They are a refuge for everyone
challenge.explanation: Vanity suggests something fleeting and insubstantial.
challenge.q: What does the image of vanity teach about people and wealth?

answers: They are exceedingly light and insubstantial
challenge.explanation: They are described as lighter than vanity when placed in the balance.
challenge.q: What does the balance image suggest about people?

answers: Do not rely on material things or human power
challenge.explanation: The passage presents human status, violence, robbery, and riches as unreliable supports.
challenge.q: What priority is implied by this passage?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “power belongeth unto God.”
The verse says, “unto thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy.”
easy.q: What belongs to the Lord according to the final verse?

easy.explanation: God renders to every man according to his work.
easy.q: How does God render to every man?

answers: Because power belongs to Him, He can judge and render according to deeds
Because He is weak, He depends on wealth
Because He hides deeds, there is no judgment
medium.explanation: God’s power is connected with His authority to render to each person according to his work.
medium.q: What is the relationship between God’s power and His judgment?

medium.explanation: The verse identifies power and authority as belonging to God.
medium.q: What does “power” mean in this passage?

answers: A person is judged according to his works
medium.explanation: The final statement says that God renders to every man according to his work.
medium.q: What moral principle appears at the end of the psalm?

answers: God is merciful while also responding to human works
Mercy removes all meaning from actions
challenge.explanation: The conclusion mentions both God’s mercy and His rendering according to each person’s work.
challenge.q: How are mercy and judgment brought together in the conclusion?

answers: The importance and certainty of the message heard
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes the declaration that power belongs to God.

answers: Those who do not trust oppression or riches remember that judgment belongs to God
Wealth becomes the source of judgment
challenge.explanation: The psalm turns people away from unreliable wealth and human power toward God’s authority and judgment.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the warning about wealth and the psalm’s conclusion?
